name: Mythology trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about myths and legends from cultures around the world. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: In Norse myth, which giantess bore the monstrous wolf Fenrir to Loki?
items.explain: Fenrir was the son of Loki and the giantess Angrboða. She also bore Jörmungandr and Hel to Loki.

items.question: Before the gods made Gleipnir, which two iron fetters did Fenrir tear apart?
items.explain: The gods tried to bind Fenrir twice with huge metal chains, Leyding and Dromi, and he broke both. Gleipnir was the third binding and the one that held.

items.question: According to one retelling of the binding of Fenrir, which of these was among the impossible ingredients the dwarves used to make Gleipnir?
items.explain: Gleipnir was made from impossible things such as the sound of a cat's footsteps, the roots of a mountain and the breath of a fish. The other options are not on the list.

source.title: Fenrir: The Monstrous Wolf of Norse Mythology

items.question: While Loki lies bound beneath a dripping serpent, what does his wife Sigyn do?
answers: She shields his face with her cloak
She sings to keep the snake asleep
She holds a bowl to catch the venom
She gnaws at the bonds that hold him
items.correct: She holds a bowl to catch the venom
items.explain: Sigyn holds a bowl over Loki's head to catch the venom that drips from the snake.

items.question: Fenrir's byname Vánagandr means "monster of the River" what?
items.explain: Vánagandr is Old Norse for "monster of the [River] Ván", one of several names for Fenrir.

items.question: In the Gilgamesh flood narrative, which god warns Utnapishtim and tells him to build a ship?
items.explain: Utnapishtim was forewarned by Ea (Enki) and survived by building a great ship.

source.title: The Flood Narrative From the Gilgamesh Epic

items.question: Which guardian of the Cedar Forest do Gilgamesh and Enkidu kill in the Epic of Gilgamesh?
items.explain: Together Gilgamesh and Enkidu kill Humbaba, the ferocious guardian of the Cedar Forest, and bring back valuable timber.

source.title: Biblical Archaeology Society - The Epic of Gilgamesh

items.question: After Gilgamesh resists her seduction, which goddess sends the Bull of Heaven to kill him?
items.explain: Ishtar sought revenge after Gilgamesh rejected her and sent the Bull of Heaven against him. Enkidu helped him kill it.

source.title: Biblical Archaeology Society - The Epic of Gilgamesh

items.question: Who is the boatman in Utnapishtim's service who takes Gilgamesh to Utnapishtim's domain?
items.explain: Urshanabi is described as a boatman serving the flood hero Utnapishtim. He ferries Gilgamesh to Utnapishtim and later goes with him back to Uruk.

items.question: In the Babylonian Enuma Elish, from the blood of which slain god does Marduk create mankind?
items.explain: Marduk makes humankind from the blood of Kingu, Tiamat's lover and the leader of her armies.

source.title: Enuma Elish: Discover the Babylonian Poem of Creation

items.question: In the Enuma Elish, the Tigris and Euphrates rivers flow from which part of Tiamat's body after Marduk kills her?
items.explain: After Marduk splits Tiamat in two with an arrow, the waters of the Tigris and Euphrates flow from her eyes.

source.title: Enuma Elish - The Babylonian Epic of Creation - Full Text - World History Encyclopedia

items.question: In the Aztec myth of Huitzilopochtli's conception, what does Coatlicue find and place in her waistband?
items.explain: Coatlicue found a ball of feathers and tucked it into her waistband. She then became pregnant with Huitzilopochtli.

items.question: On which mount does Coatlicue give birth to Huitzilopochtli, who then defeats his brothers?
items.explain: Coatlicue gave birth on Mount Coatepec, pursued by her children. The newborn Huitzilopochtli, born armed, defeated most of his brothers there.

items.question: Which blue serpent does the newborn Huitzilopochtli use to kill his half-sister Coyolxauhqui?
items.explain: Huitzilopochtli tore out Coyolxauhqui's heart using Xiuhcoatl, a blue snake, and threw her body down the mountain.

items.question: Which three animals combine to form the Egyptian devourer Ammit, who waits beside the scales of judgment?
items.explain: Ammit is a composite creature that is part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus.

items.question: In the Egyptian Weighing of the Heart, which god records the verdict?
items.explain: Thoth is the god who records the verdict of the Weighing of the Heart.

items.question: Which Book of the Dead spell was often inscribed on heart scarabs placed with the deceased?
items.explain: Spell 30 was often inscribed on heart scarabs. The weighing of the heart itself is described in spell 125.

source.title: The book of death: weighing your heart

items.question: In the Kojiki, the birth of which fire deity fatally wounds Izanami?
items.explain: According to the Kojiki, the fire deity Kagu-tsuchi burned Izanami at birth and wounded her fatally.

items.question: According to the Kojiki, Amaterasu was born when Izanagi purified which part of himself?
items.explain: In the Kojiki, Izanagi produced Amaterasu when he purified his left eye after returning from the underworld.

items.question: In what year was the Kojiki, a Japanese chronicle of ancient myths, recorded?
items.explain: The Kojiki was recorded in 712 CE. The Nihon Shoki, which is often confused with it, followed in 720 CE.

items.question: Which three sacred emblems associated with Amaterasu are symbols of the Japanese imperial throne?
answers: A mirror, a bow and a drum
A fan, a sword and a bell
A spear, a jewel and a fan
A mirror, a sword and a jewel
items.correct: A mirror, a sword and a jewel
items.explain: The three emblems are the sacred mirror, the sword of Susanoo and the jewel from the cave myth. They symbolize the Japanese empire.

items.question: Which of the Tuatha Dé Danann's four great treasures is said to cry out when the rightful king of Ireland stands on it?
items.explain: The Stone of Destiny (Lia Fáil) cries out under the rightful king of Ireland. The spear always hits its mark and the sword could never be defeated.

items.question: Through his mother, the Irish hero-god Lugh is grandson of which Fomorian leader?
items.explain: Lugh is the grandson of the Fomorian leader Balor through his mother, even though he is a champion of the Tuatha Dé Danann.

source.title: The Tuatha Dé Danann: The Supernatural Race of Irish Mythology

items.question: In the Lebor Gabála Érenn (Book of Invasions), which wave of settlers are the Tuatha Dé Danann?
items.explain: The Book of Invasions presents the Tuatha Dé Danann as the fifth wave of settlers to arrive in Ireland.

source.title: Celtic Gods & Goddesses of Ireland: Dagda, Morrígan and Brigid

items.question: Which Milesian poet calmed the sea after the Tuatha Dé Danann raised a magical storm against the invaders?
items.explain: The Milesian poet Amergin calmed the sea with his verse. His people then landed and defeated the Tuatha Dé Danann.

items.question: Which mountain served as the churning rod when the gods and demons churned the Ocean of Milk?
items.explain: In the Samudra Manthan the mountain Mandara, also called Mandaragiri, was used as the churning rod.

source.title: Samudra Manthan - the Churning of Our Inner Consciousness

items.question: After drinking the poison halahala that emerged from the churning of the ocean, which epithet did Shiva earn?
items.explain: Shiva drank the poison halahala to save creation. His throat turned blue, which earned him the name Nilakantha ("Blue Throat").

items.question: In which avatar did Vishnu dive beneath the sinking Mandara mountain and bear it on his back during the churning of the ocean?
items.explain: Vishnu took the form of a huge tortoise, the Kurma avatar, and carried the mountain on his back so the churning could continue.

source.title: Samudra Manthan - the Churning of Our Inner Consciousness

items.question: Which serpent king was used as the churning rope in the Samudra Manthan?
items.explain: The gods and demons invited Vasuki, king of the snakes, to serve as the churning cord. He was tied around Mount Mandara.

source.title: Samudra Manthan: Churning the Ocean for the Elixir of Immortality - Glorious Hinduism

items.question: In the Popol Vuh, the Hero Twins' mother Xquic is the daughter of which lord of Xibalba?
items.explain: In the Popol Vuh, Xquic is the daughter of Cuchumaquic, one of the Lords of Xibalba. She becomes the mother of Hunahpu and Xbalanque.

items.question: Which pretentious bird demon do the Maya Hero Twins destroy in the Popol Vuh?
items.explain: Besides their conquest of Xibalba, the Twins destroy the pretentious bird demon Vucub Caquix and his two demonic sons.

items.question: What does the name of the Maya underworld Xibalba mean?
items.explain: Xibalba means "Place of Fear". It was a layered underworld ruled by twelve death gods led by Hun Came and Vucub Came.

source.title: Mayan Mythology: The Complete Guide to the Popol Vuh, the Hero Twins, and the Maya Underworld

items.question: After defeating the Lords of Death, what do the Hero Twins become in the Popol Vuh narrative?
items.explain: In the Popol Vuh narrative, the Twins ascend to the sky after defeating the Lords of Death and become the sun and the moon.

source.title: Maya Hero Twins: Defeating the Lords of Death

items.question: From what is Māui's magical fishhook traditionally carved in Polynesian myth?
items.explain: Māui's magical fishhook is traditionally said to be carved from the jawbone of his grandmother.

source.title: Polynesian Creation Myths: Ever Wondered How Hawai'i Was Created?

items.question: In Māori tradition, Te Ika-a-Māui, the great fish that Māui hauled from the sea, is which landmass?
items.explain: Māui used a magical fishhook to pull Te Ika-a-Māui, New Zealand's North Island, from the seafloor.

source.title: Who Is Māui in Polynesian Mythology?

items.question: Which fire goddess does Māui trick into giving up her fingernails of flame?
items.explain: Māui tricks the fire goddess Mahuika into giving up her fingernails of flame. Fire then takes refuge in certain trees, where people make it by friction.

source.title: Polynesian Mythology: Māui, Pele, Rangi & Papa

items.question: In Hawaiian myth, the fire goddess Pele's quarrels with which sea-goddess sister help shape the islands?
items.explain: Pele, the fire goddess, and her sister Nāmaka, the sea goddess, hated each other. Their battles formed parts of the Hawaiian Islands.

source.title: Polynesian Creation Myths: Ever Wondered How Hawai'i Was Created?

items.question: In Hesiod's account, which beings were born from drops of Uranus's blood that fell on the Earth after Cronus castrated him?
items.explain: From the drops of Uranus's blood that fell upon the earth came the Erinyes, the Giants and the Meliad nymphs. Aphrodite came from the foam around the severed genitals.

source.title: Castration of Uranus - Greek Mythology Link

items.question: Which mountain served as the base of the older generation of gods, the Titans, during the Titanomachy?
items.explain: The Titans were based on Mount Othrys. The Olympians who fought them would come to reign on Mount Olympus.

items.question: Which Titan, a son of Iapetus, was second in command to Cronus during the Titanomachy?
items.explain: Atlas, another son of Iapetus, was second in command after Cronus in the war against the Olympians.

items.question: To which island did Rhea flee, with help from Gaia and Uranus, to give birth to Zeus?
items.explain: Rhea appealed to Gaia and Uranus for help and was helped to escape to Crete, where Zeus was born, so that Cronus could not swallow him.

items.question: Which figure from the Hittite "Kingship in Heaven" text offers an Anatolian parallel to Hesiod's Uranus–Cronus castration conflict?
items.explain: The Hittite Kingship in Heaven text, with its castration motif, offers in Kumarbi an Anatolian parallel to Hesiod's conflict between Uranus and Cronus.

items.question: In Slavic tree imagery, which bird represents the thunder god Perun in the crown while the serpent Veles lurks at the roots?
items.explain: Perun is portrayed as an eagle sitting in the crown of the tree. The serpentine Veles is at the roots, in the Underworld.

items.question: Which Slavic deity is the divine smith of celestial fire and the sky?
items.explain: Svarog is the Slavic god of celestial fire and the sky, the divine smith whose forge produces the celestial fire.

source.title: Slavic Mythology: Gods, Creatures, and the Tradition That Never Quite Went Away

items.question: In one version of the Chang'e myth, who tries to get Hou Yi's immortality pill before Chang'e swallows it?
items.explain: Chang'e swallowed the pill before Feng Meng could get it. She then became immortal and flew to the moon.

items.question: The story of Pangu separating heaven and earth first appears in written sources from which century CE?
items.explain: Nüwa's sky repair and Houyi's ten suns are preserved in the 2nd-century BCE Huainanzi. The Pangu story first appears in writings of the 3rd century CE.

source.title: Chinese Mythology: Pangu, Nüwa & Sun Wukong

items.question: In Ferdowsi's Shahnameh, in which mountain is the serpent-shouldered tyrant Zahhak finally chained by Fereydun?
items.explain: Fereydun overthrows Zahhak and chains him inside Mount Damavand.

source.title: Zahhak: Persian Myth's Serpent-Shouldered Tyrant King

items.question: In the Shahnameh, the hero Rostam is the son of Rudaba and which father?
items.explain: Rostam is the son of Zāl and Rudaba. The Simurgh, which had raised Zāl, later helped at Rostam's birth.

source.title: Shahnameh The Epic of The Persian Kings

items.question: What does the blacksmith Kaveh use as a banner to rally the revolt against Zahhak in the Shahnameh?
items.explain: Kaveh uses his smith's leather apron as a banner. He then seeks out Fereydun and helps him overthrow Zahhak.

items.question: In the Yoruba creation legend, the first mound of earth at Oke Ora, from which Ife was built, formed from soil in what?
items.explain: In the Yoruba creation legend, Oke Ora was the first mound of earth, formed from the soil in a snail shell. Ife, the first settlement, was built from it.
